t.1.136.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But Purocana, seeing them cheerful after they had dwelt there a full year, and perceiving them to be, as it were, trusting, rejoiced.
t.1.136.2: When Purocana was thus delighted, Kaunteya Yudhiṣṭhira, the knower of dharma, then spoke to Bhīmasena and Arjuna, and to the twins as well.
t.1.136.3: This wicked Purocana believes that we trust him completely. This cruel-hearted man has been deceived; I think it is the time for flight.
t.1.136.4: Having set fire to the armoury and burned Purocana as well, and having placed six living beings here, let us flee unnoticed.
t.1.136.5: Then, O king, under the pretext of giving gifts, Kuntī held a great feast for the brāhmaṇas at night, and women came there.
t.1.136.7: But to that feast, by chance, a Niṣāda woman with five sons came, seeking food, she and her sons, driven by fate.
t.1.136.6: Those women, having enjoyed themselves as they pleased, having eaten and drunk, O Bhārata, took leave of Mādhavī and went back to their homes at night.
t.1.136.8: Having drunk the liquor, she, intoxicated and reeling with drunkenness, together with her sons, with all her sons, O king, fell asleep in that very house, senseless and like one dead, O lord of men.
t.1.136.9: Then, O lord, in the night, when a violent wind was blowing and the people were asleep, Bhīma set fire to that place where Purocana was sleeping.
t.1.136.10: Then a very great heat and roar of the fire arose, and by that the crowd of people awoke.
t.1.136.12: Alas, shame! The mind of Dhṛtarāṣṭra is not at all righteous, he who had the pure young Pāṇḍavas burned by his minister.
t.1.136.11: The house that the wicked, foolish man employed by Duryodhana had built and then set on fire has brought about his own destruction.
t.1.136.13: But now, by good fortune, this evil-souled, utterly wicked-minded one has been burned, he who burned those best of men, the blameless ones who trusted him completely.
t.1.136.14: Thus the people of Vāraṇāvata lamented, and, surrounding that house, they stood on every side throughout the night.
t.1.136.15: And those Pāṇḍavas too, O king, deeply distressed, went forth with their mother through that tunnel and departed in secret, unseen.
t.1.136.16: Because of that obstruction of sleep and because of their fear, the Pāṇḍavas, scorchers of their foes, were unable to set out hastily together with their mother.
t.1.136.17: But Bhīmasena, O king of kings, whose speed and prowess were terrible, went forth carrying all his brothers and his mother as well.
t.1.136.18: The mighty one, having lifted his mother onto his shoulder and the twins onto his hip, and taking in his two hands his two exceedingly strong brothers, the Pārthas,
t.1.136.19: Breaking the trees with his force and rending the earth with his two feet, the mighty Vṛkodara, swift as the wind, went on quickly.
